clue.text: What loser's not — awfully capable

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters of the preceding words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, with the S of the possessive counted as a letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jibe that whatever a loser lacks, it is not dreadful ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' is the anagram signal for the thirteen letters of WHAT LOSERS NOT; here the apostrophe's S is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deserving their pay is competent, which is what capable means.

clue.text: To be in control, cross-dress?

definitions.meaning: to be the one in charge, especially in a marriage
to put on clothing of the opposite sex, here men's legwear

explanation.surface: Taking charge likened to dressing in clothes of the other sex.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for being the dominant partner, read literally, describes a woman putting on men's legwear; the question mark flags the literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means holding authority in a household; read literally it is putting on male garments, a form of cross-dressing.

clue.text: Quickly make an approach

definitions.meaning: to ... a garment is to sew it hastily
the sprint before a jump or a bowler's delivery

explanation.definitionFit: To run up clothes is to sew them fast; a run-up is the approaching sprint before a leap or delivery.

clue.text: Teaching post attached to school in which child is nourished

indicators.note: the professorship is fixed onto the end of the school word, so it follows it

parts.note: a high school is a secondary school, so HIGH stands in for school
a chair is a professorship at a university

explanation.surface: A professor's job joined to a school, where a child is fed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall seat with a tray where infants are fed their meals.

clue.text: Palindromic form this brief communication takes on?

definitions.text: Palindromic form this brief communication takes on?

parts.words: Palindromic form this brief communication takes on?
parts.note: a short written message; read backwards its letters nearly echo themselves, a playful hint at a near palindrome

explanation.walkthrough: A cryptic definition: the answer is a short letter, and the clue teases that the word almost reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A small folded card used for a short written message is a brief communication.

clue.text: Juice from plants I had found palatable

parts.note: sap is the fluid circulating in plants
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone found the plant juice tasted pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a pleasing flavour; the word is a literary synonym for tasty.

clue.text: It describes onset of consternation in plane going into a headlong descent

indicators.note: the aircraft with its added letter is put inside the plunging phrase

parts.note: a dive is a steep headlong plunge

indicators.note: the first letter of consternation sits within the aircraft word

parts.note: a jet is a jet-propelled aircraft

indicators.note: the start of consternation gives its first letter only

explanation.surface: Panic aboard a plane as it plunges into a nosedive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It describes' looks like the start of a story about a plane, but it is the definition: the word class that qualifies nouns. 'in' and 'going into' nest the pieces one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A part of speech whose job is to qualify a noun, giving a description of it.

clue.text: In panic, I start to tremble — I fear an unknown force

indicators.note: the first two pieces are placed within the word for panic

parts.note: terror is extreme panic
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of tremble gives its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
alarm is sudden fear
Y is a conventional unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Someone panicking, starting to shake, confesses fear of a mysterious enemy force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' at the start signals that the I and the T go inside the panic word. The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve force, so 'force' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The British volunteer reserve of the army, a military body or force.

clue.text: Heard parent curse

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for parent is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, a parent

explanation.surface: A parent overheard swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild oath or swear word, an expletive used as a curse.

clue.text: Rise from one's bed and dress

definitions.meaning: to get out of bed in the morning
an outfit, often a showy or odd costume

explanation.surface: Someone climbing out of bed and putting clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means to rise in the morning; as a hyphenated noun it is an outfit or costume.

clue.text: Makeshift panel in box

definitions.meaning: as in ...-rigged or ... mast, improvised for temporary use
the twelve people seated in a courtroom's ... box

explanation.surface: A temporary group of people seated in an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors' jury rigs are improvised; the group of jurors in a court box is a panel.

clue.text: A clay-pit dug out of the common

indicators.note: dug suggests earth turned over, so these letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clay pit excavated on village common land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of the common' looks like part of the digging picture, but it is the definition, meaning unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Not typical, so unusual or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Member of gang — lawyer takes care of it

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, a US lawyer
c/o is the abbreviation for care of in addresses
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gangster's lawyer agrees to look after something.
explanation.walkthrough: A dacoit is a member of an armed robber band in India or Burma.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian or Burmese armed robber operating in a band, so one of a gang.

clue.text: He needs intelligence to keep in control

parts.note: a head for things is brains or intelligence
to master is to subdue or keep under control

explanation.surface: A man needs brains to keep order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the definition, a teasing stand-in for the person in charge of a school; 'needs' links the brains and the control pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The man in charge of a school is referred to as 'he' in this whole-clue picture of school discipline.

clue.text: Broadcasting, press switches in clock

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are put inside the clock face word

parts.note: a dial is a clock face, slang for a clock

indicators.note: switches means the letters change places

explanation.surface: Press reports of switches broadcast inside a clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switches' reshuffles the letters of press into SPERS, and 'in' sets them inside the clock face. Broadcasting here means scattering seed by hand, not radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Scattering or spreading widely, as seed is broadcast by hand.

clue.text: Perfume of a sort we're developing

indicators.note: developing means evolving into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some kind of scent that we are working on.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant liquid distilled from petals, used as a scent or flavouring.

clue.text: One man joined club

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A single man becoming a club member.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf club with a metal head is called by this name.

clue.text: Flag, something like a rainbow

definitions.meaning: a yellow flag is a wild plant of this kind
the coloured ring of the eye, named for the Greek goddess of the rainbow

explanation.definitionFit: The yellow flag is a flower of this genus; the name means rainbow in Greek, apt for the coloured ring of the eye.

clue.text: Restaurant possessed by heiress — it originally faced the other way

indicators.note: the held letters are read from right to left
the run of letters is held within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: An heiress owns an eatery that once looked the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possessed by' finds EIRESSITOR inside 'heiress — it originally', and 'faced the other way' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant specialising in meat roasted on a turning spit takes its name from the spit.

clue.text: Man holding heavy weight up — and vice versa

definitions.text: Man holding heavy weight up — and vice versa

indicators.note: the weight word holds the other piece inside it, the roles swapped by vice versa

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: male stands in for man

explanation.surface: A man lifts a great weight, and the weight in turn holds him.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, the clue defines a sculpted male figure supporting a load. 'and vice versa' swaps the roles: TON holds MALE written upwards, ELAM.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture this is a carved male figure used as a column, bearing the load above.

clue.text: I have found it at the back of the menu, near the Greek moussaka

indicators.note: the back of each word is its final letter, so the last letters are taken

explanation.surface: A diner spotting moussaka at the bottom of a Greek menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of' takes the last letter of each of the six words, starting with 'the' before 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek exclamation attributed to Archimedes means precisely that he had found something.

clue.text: Warning in jolly fashion

parts.note: a la is French for in the fashion of, the 'in' completing the phrase
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: A warning delivered in a cheerful manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... fashion' is À LA wrapped round 'jolly', which gives RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal or bell giving notice of danger is a warning.

clue.text: Left very much within one's rights

parts.note: awfully is a colloquial intensifier meaning very much

explanation.surface: Departing a great deal while legally entitled.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting legitimately, as permitted under the law.

clue.text: Turn up to catch game in city

indicators.note: in a down entry, turn up means the pieces are written bottom to top

parts.note: to nab is to catch
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Turning up to watch a match in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' reverses the whole of NAB plus RU, giving the answer from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to or situated in a town, as opposed to the country.

clue.text: Competitive pair embracing their opponents could make this

definitions.text: Competitive pair embracing their opponents could make this

indicators.note: the bridge partnership wraps around the opposing partnership

parts.note: North and South are one partnership at the bridge table
East and West oppose North and South at bridge

explanation.surface: Rivals hugging one another would be worth reporting.
explanation.walkthrough: At bridge, N and S sit opposite each other and play against E and W.
explanation.definitionFit: Reports of recent events; an unexpected embrace of rivals would be newsworthy.

clue.text: Allow daughter into a US university

indicators.note: the daughter letter is put inside the university

parts.note: A plus MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Letting a daughter enrol at an American university.
explanation.definitionFit: To let in or grant entry, so permit.

clue.text: Produced member of Byronic tribe

definitions.meaning: past tense of bear, as in gave birth to
Byron's Don Juan divides society into two tribes, the tedious people and the wearied ones

explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of bear means gave birth; Byron called society two tribes, the tedious ones and the wearied.

clue.text: Sadly only dog mourns man buried on Sunday

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters are put into a disordered state

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lone dog grieves for its master laid to rest on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: Solomon Grundy is the nursery-rhyme character born on a Monday and buried on Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme this figure is born on Monday and laid in the grave on Sunday.
